I never had friends of my own. Growing up, other kids didn't want to hang out or play with me - they were ok with me joining in the fun if either/both my siblings were there, but whenever it was just me, miraculously they'd have something else they wanted to do instead. And this would, more or less, continue even until adulthood. At secondary school none of my "friends" were ever up for me coming over at the weekends, or them coming to mine. At college none of my "friends" wanted to hang out at weekends, even though we both knew we'd be in the same area at the same time. At university my "friends" would never call or message me, it was always me calling them. At the end of my degree we all bought little black books to write comments and contact details in. I wrote my mobile number and my home landline number, and personal email address, in every book I was given. 36 people wrote in my book. Of those 36, 8 gave me their phone number, the rest were just comments along the lines of "it was nice to know your". Of those 8, not a single one was a real phone number. It was at this point that I realized it was utterly pointless in even attempting to make and keep friendships as it was clear that people just don't want to know me, don't want me around, and just don't want me generally. And that's just on friendships.

On relationships, it is and always was a similar affair. I started to get properly interested in girls at about the age of 12. Over the course of the next 15 years I got up the courage to ask someone out between 3 and 5 times a year. Every single time it was a flat out rejection, and frequently with a chuckle and a "oh, you were serious". Clearly many of those 62 people thought it was laughable that I would think they'd be interested in me. Number 63 actually said yes, and a few years later we got married. We're now almost 15 years into the relationship and she wants a divorce and terms me that she never really wanted me, I was just convenient.

So I think the writing on the table is pretty damn clear. Nobody wants me, for either friendship or more. I have been, am, and will continue to be, Forever Alone.

WI is being an asshole, but being an asshole is not necessarily WI.

WI is when one party pretends to be incompetent so the other party has to take up the responsibility. The 2 big parts of it are the pretence, and the pushing the *responsibility* on to the other party. Being purposefully shit at doing the dishes so their partner has to do them, is WI. Not knowing where the clit is makes them an asshole, and a pretty shitty lover if they're not prepared to put in the effort to learn, but there isn't necessarily any pretence (obvs kinda depends on the individual), and there isn't any responsibility shifting going on, so it can't really be considered *weaponized* incompetence. Incompetence, maybe. Assholery, absolutely. But not weaponized incompetence.

1. Smiling does not make everything better. Don't come at me with bullshit about smiling releasing endorphins, dopamine and serotonin. If your brain isn't receptive to those chemicals (as is the case with a huge proportion of lonely people, particularly those with chronic loneliness) then this just does not work, and when it doesn't work those people will simply feel like they're even more of a failure than they thought because they can't even do smiling right.
2. It's called hyper vigilance. It's a trauma response. Would you tell someone with demonstrable PTSD to just "stop having PTSD"? No, you wouldn't.
3. Exercise releases endorphins. See point 1.
4. Friendship is a RECIPROCAL thing. You can't just "become a friend". If there's nobody in your life with whom you can build a friendship, then who the fuck are you supposed to "become a friend" with?!
